mappings.note: Whom the chidiya stands for, keyed literally as 'birds' -- a point recovered from the poem. Rejected CG-HIN3, which I keep for the item whose key is the symbolic reading.
Who works all day (the birds) -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-118: no idea is being weighed.
Which bird 'shuk' names (the parrot) -- a literary bird name to be glossed. Rejected LO-121: the demand is lexical.
Which bird 'kapot' names (the pigeon) -- a literary bird name. Rejected LO-121 on the same ground.
What she tells the bound man (the mukti-mantra) -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-124, kept for the item that glosses that phrase.
Who sings on the high peepal branch. Rejected LO-115: a fact, not a scene to render.
Who teaches the way of love (the chidiya). Rejected LO-118: the agent, not the idea.
Sense of 'sone ki kadiyaan', keyed as greed and bondage -- a metaphor to be unpacked. Rejected LO-121: no line states it.
Which feeling the poet asks man to give up (droh) -- named in the verse. Rejected LO-124, kept for the item glossing that word.
What she tells in her own speech -- a message of love and unity, which the poem leaves to be read. Rejected LO-121: no line says it outright.
Which way she teaches (prem-preeti) -- quoted from the verse. Rejected LO-124, kept for the gloss item.
What she tells the world's bound man -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-118: stated.
Which birds live together in the forest -- the poem's list. Rejected LO-124: the names are quoted, not glossed.
Where the birds' home is (the sky). Rejected LO-118, kept for the item asking what that implies.
What the birds' minds lack -- greed, sin, care: quoted from the line. Rejected LO-118: stated.
How the birds fill themselves -- by their own labour, as the poem says. Rejected LO-118: stated.
What the chidiya asks man to learn (to live unfettered) -- the poet's idea behind her speech. Rejected LO-121: no line puts it this way.

Which feeling the line conveys (attraction) -- reading the mood of a quoted line. Rejected LO-121: the mood is inferred. NOTE: the quoted line 'varsha-bahaar sabke man ko lubha rahi hai' belongs to the Varsha-Bahaar poem, not to Chidiya -- this item is filed in the wrong chapter.

What the chidiya SYMBOLISES, keyed as freedom, simplicity and love -- reading a poetic pratik. Cited at goal level because no outcome among the 16 covers poetic symbol: LO-122 is folk song and tale specifically, and LO-124 concerns the learner's own use of words.
Sense of 'jag ke bandi maanav' -- a figure to be unpacked as man caught in worldly attachment. Rejected LO-121: no line defines it.
The poem's main message -- its usefulness read off the whole. Rejected LO-118: the message itself, not his handling of an idea.

Blank is the compound 'seema-heen' -- a literary formation. Rejected LO-121 on the same ground.

What the chidiya means by the line about giving up enmity -- the poet's idea put in her mouth. Rejected LO-124, kept for the item that glosses 'droh-bhaavna' itself.
Where the chidiya sits -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-115: a fact, not a rendering.
How the poem characterises the birds' life -- simple, selfless, content: a reading rather than a quotation. Rejected LO-121 for that reason.
